tldr: DeepSeek open-sourced DeepInfer, the inference engine behind its production services, on Oct 20. On Oct 31 it published the architecture of an always-on coding agent, dsh-superagent.
whats_new: Coverage of the dsh-superagent prototype, a router-worker coding agent that watches team chat for work, continued through Nov 4, while the rest of the thread is third-party inference-engine news.
why_it_matters: DeepSeek is releasing both the serving layer (DeepInfer, reportedly 155T tokens/day) and an agent harness, so platform teams can inspect a production-scale stack, but the cost and throughput figures come from DeepSeek and press reports, not independent benchmarks.

status.detail: Two DeepSeek open-source drops, DeepInfer and dsh-superagent, with no independent benchmarks yet.

beats.headline: DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer, its production inference engine
beats.summary: Wide press pickup of the engine, with claims of 155T tokens a day per cluster.

beats.headline: Loosely related research and framework papers clustered in
beats.summary: Mostly arXiv and discussion items that share keywords with the thread rather than reporting on DeepSeek.

beats.headline: dsh-superagent: a router-worker coding agent goes open source
beats.summary: Positioned against Claude Code; works from team chat.

beats.headline: Other inference engines and serving economics in the same window
beats.summary: llm-d 1.0, Nvidia Flare, XLA Serving Engine and hosting-profitability discussion.

open_questions: Will anyone publish independent throughput or cost benchmarks of DeepInfer outside DeepSeek's own figures?
Which models and hardware does DeepInfer support beyond DeepSeek's own?
Is dsh-superagent usable beyond a research prototype, and under what license?
take_for_builders: Before adopting DeepInfer or dsh-superagent, check license terms and hardware support, and benchmark them against your current serving stack rather than relying on the quoted token-per-day numbers.
